rule: Runbook criterion 11: every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict; no barrier is crossed with an open NOT DISCHARGED; and every 'behaviour the commit bodies do not mention' finding is either documented or reverted. R-35's mechanism was real and used throughout the campaign -- commit bodies across the range cite verify-P2b and verify-P5-retire findings and answer six NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts themselves were only ever written into commit bodies, so 'every slice has a recorded verdict' could not be checked from the repository. That is the first half of the criterion and it is the half this file exists to start.
what_this_ledger_does_not_hold: The verdicts of the campaign's earlier slices. They are recoverable only by reading the commit bodies that answer them, one range at a time, and reconstructing them here from those bodies would be this campaign's own failure shape -- a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. So the ledger starts where a lane could record a verdict honestly, which is the pass that produced it, and the gap for everything before it is stated rather than papered over. A campaign that ran this file from slice one would have the criterion; this one has the mechanism and one pass.

passes.what_this_round_is: A second independent R-35 pass over the slice group round 4 covered, run because round 4 closed with a criterion still NOT_DISCHARGED and a disposition of documented_open. It returned that criterion unchanged and five further findings of behaviour the commit bodies do not mention -- two of them re-measurements of rows round 4 already carries, confirmed accurate rather than corrected, and one a confirmation that the three fixes round 4 cites are real in the tree and not merely narrated. What is new in this round is the structural half. Round 4's own note named the cause -- campaign bookkeeping declared inside a runtime module -- and left it unpaid on the argument that paying it 'cannot discharge this criterion in any case'. That argument is true about the measurement and is not a reason to leave the cause standing, so the cause is paid here and the measurement is recorded as still failing.

criteria.what_was_found: Re-measured rather than read off round 4: git diff --stat 0248a42^..b19a577 -- src/ returns src/calculator/interpreters/__init__.py, 11 insertions / 10 deletions, and the same diff over 0248a42^..HEAD was identical when this round ran, so no commit had reverted it. 4876eb2 adds `from dataclasses import replace`, the module constant _CLOSEOUT and _AMP_WALK_LANE, and turns UnservedLane.retires_at into a per-lane conditional in two dict comprehensions plus three hand-spelled sites. Every mitigation round 4 lists is still true and none of them is what the criterion says. The verdict stands.
criteria.note: The cause is paid and the measurement still fails, and those are two different sentences. Paid: 8e36c60 removes retires_at from interpreters.UnservedLane entirely. src/ now declares the two facts about the tree a reader can check at import -- which interpreter produces the number, and by which lane -- and no stage at all; every unserved lane's retiring stage is resolved from the one stage record that declares itself the creditor_of that lane's debt, so a ruled re-dating is an edit to docs/receipts/campaign-stages.json alone. Measured after: git grep -n retires_at -- src/ returns nothing, against 6 occurrences before, and tests/test_behavior_frontier.py::test_no_campaign_stage_is_declared_anywhere_under_src asserts against source that no stage name any committed record declares appears anywhere under src/ and that UnservedLane's fields are exactly {reason, via}. Still failing: the criterion quantifies over four landed commits, and the only edit that would empty git diff 0248a42^..HEAD -- src/ is restoring the module to its 0248a42^ blob. That was considered and is refused for a reason and not for the cost. The blob dates the fourteen rows to 'Phase 4 S3 -- one kernel, five views', which Amendment K re-dated them OFF and Amendment F measured cannot perform the retiring act, so the runtime module would carry a superseded dating in the present tense; and because the gate binds the tree's declaration to the recorded stage, keeping it green would additionally take editing that clause. A false statement in src/, or a weakened gate, bought so that a measurement reads as a pass, is the ordering this campaign exists to invert -- the ledger's round-3 precedent refuses the same trade in the other direction, 'reverting a correct pin to satisfy an ownership sentence'. So the record is: the four commits changed src/, that is history and cannot be un-landed, and from 8e36c60 no future ruling can repeat it.

coverage.rule: Runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict -- had no denominator. 'Every slice' bounded nothing a machine could read, so a ledger holding one pass and a ledger holding forty were indistinguishable to every gate. This block is the denominator, derived from the tree rather than authored: the campaign's own slice labels, which are the trailing parenthetical tag each lane stamped on its commit subjects.
coverage.how_the_population_is_derived: The first element of the trailing parenthetical of every commit subject in 584071e..HEAD. A commit whose subject carries no such tag is counted in untagged_commits and reported rather than dropped -- a slice that never labelled itself is a hole in the convention, not an absence of slices.
coverage.what_this_block_does_not_do: It does not reconstruct a verdict. The earlier passes' verdicts live only in the commit bodies that answer them, and rebuilding them here from those bodies would be a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently -- the reason the ledger began mid-campaign. What is recorded is whether a slice group has a verdict IN THIS LEDGER, which is a fact about this file and is checkable without reading a single body. What it now DOES do is grade the residue instead of collapsing it: a slice group whose own commits record an R-35 verdict, naming the mechanism and carrying a verdict word, is listed by name under slice_groups_citing_a_verdict_in_a_commit_body (by name and not by sha: the ledger is committed inside the commit a sha would point at, so a sha here goes stale the moment that commit is amended). That is deliberately weaker than a recorded verdict -- a commit body is the LANE's transcription of the verifier's answer, not the verifier's artifact -- and it is a strict subset of the groups with none here, never a substitute. Collapsing 'a citation a reader can open' with 'nothing at all' is what made a ledger holding one pass and a ledger holding forty look alike to every gate.
coverage.what_the_residue_buys: Two things the criterion never had. The gap is a number that cannot grow in silence, the way the sole-home scan made criterion 4's residue a number. And the gate asserts the derived tag set equals these two lists -- so the NEXT slice group cannot ship without either a verdict row or an explicit line in slice_groups_without_one. Going forward the clause holds by machine; backwards it is measured and open, which is the honest pair. The forward half fired for real on 2026-08-15: the tag campaign-close-charge-price-oracle shipped with no line here, R-01 row 1 went red on the commit that shipped it, and the two rows were added by the next lane rather than discovered by a reader. That is the clause working, and it is recorded here because a gate whose one firing goes unrecorded is indistinguishable from a gate that has never fired.
coverage.why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroac: A verify verdict is a fresh read-only agent's report on a tree at a commit. The trees are still there and the agents are not, and a verdict written now by anyone who has read the plan is not an R-35 verdict at all -- the brief's whole content is that the reader has not read the plan. So the residue closes by the campaign ending, or by re-running R-35 over the historical ranges as its own scheduled work with its own briefs. It does not close by anybody filling in this file. Restated 2026-08-14 with the number: 10 of the groups without a verdict here cite one in a commit body, and the other rows cite nothing anywhere. Closing those is 60-odd fresh R-35 passes by verifiers that have not read the plan -- not a lane's to run, not reconstructible from the commit bodies of the lanes being checked, and not closeable by shrinking the denominator. It is recorded as an owed ruling in docs/receipts/rulings-owed.json rather than as a gap in a report. Prepared 2026-08-14: the branch that binds the clause backwards is now priced and startable row by row in docs/receipts/verify-backlog.json -- which changes what the ruling costs to schedule and changes nothing about the ruling, because preparing a pass is not running one.

prepared_work.what_it_holds: One row per group in slice_groups_without_one: the commits that group spans, by subject; the plan documents that carry its stated completion criteria; and whether its own commit bodies cite an R-35 answer. The brief is not copied into it -- it is read from R-35 in the runbook at run time, so a prepared pass can never be handed a weaker brief than the ruling states.
prepared_work.what_it_is_not: Coverage. Every row is a pass that has NOT run, and the backlog says so in its own words. It answers no part of the owed ruling and shrinks no denominator: its row set is asserted equal to this list, so preparing the work cannot become a way of redefining it.
prepared_work.why_it_exists: why_the_residue_cannot_be_closed_retroactively says the residue closes by re-running R-35 over the historical ranges as scheduled work with its own briefs. No range and no brief existed anywhere in the tree, so the backwards branch of the owed ruling had a cost nobody could price beyond 'sixty-odd passes' and work nobody could begin. It now has one row per pass.
